newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel's Levy invited to see Albright.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Levy invited to see Albright.

text.p: Israeli Foreign Minister David Levy has been invited to Washington for talks on the Middle East peace process with U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright on Friday, a Foreign Ministry official said on Tuesday.
Asked if he could confirm Israel media reports that Levy would meet Albright on Friday, the official said: "In principle that is correct, that is to say there is an invitation like that."
The official, who asked not to be identified, said Levy had already been set to make a private visit to Florida on Sunday.

Levy, while neither directly confirming nor denying he would visit Washington, rejected Israeli media reports that Albright wanted to see him because the administration was disappointed in contacts with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
"It is silly and childish because I represent the government's policy and all that will be done will be in line with the policy," Levy told Israel Radio.
Israel's peacemaking with the Palestinians came to a halt when Israel broke ground for a new Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18.

Levy reaffirmed Israel would not stop building the 6,500-unit project, which has spurred West Bank clashes, nor cease construction in other existing Jewish settlements in the West Bank and Gaza Strip.

"There is no ban on building in the Oslo accords, not in Jerusalem nor in the settlements," he said, referring to the historic 1993 framework peace deal reached by Israel's previous government with the Palestinians.

Palestinians hope eventually to establish an independent state in the West Bank and Gaza with East Jerusalem as capital. They view settlement building during the interim peace deal phase as pre-empting final peace talks which have yet to occur.
